source_lines.87: 4.1 Equivariance of the polynomial lift. The extension $F$ on $X$ is equivariant: for every $g$, the two regular maps expressing equivariance agree on the dense orbit by step 1.3 and therefore on $X$. Let $E_K$ be the finite-dimensional rational module of polynomial maps $operatorname{End}(V)	ooperatorname{End}(V^{otimes d})$ of degree at most $K$, for $KgedegPhi$, with action $(gcdotPsi)(Y)=g^{otimes d}Psi(g^{-1}Yg)(g^{-1})^{otimes d}$. Let $I_Ksubset E_K$ consist of maps vanishing on $X$. Then $I_K$ is stable and the class of the lift from step 3.1 in $E_K/I_K$ is invariant. Scalar matrices act trivially on $E_K$: they conjugate neither the input nor the output. For $Nge2$, Weyl's theorem [F3] applied to the semisimple Lie algebra $mathfrak{sl}(V)$ gives an $mathfrak{sl}(V)$-stable complement to $I_K$. This complement is stable under $mathrm{SL}(V)$, since elementary matrices $exp(tE_{ij})$ generate that group and their rational representation acts by exponentiating the differential; together with scalar matrices they generate $mathrm{GL}(V)$ over $mathbb C$. For $N=1$ the whole group acts trivially, so any vector-space complement suffices. The quotient map restricted to this complement is thus a $mathrm{GL}(V)$-isomorphism and lifts the invariant class to an invariant $Phi'in E_K$. It agrees with $F$ on $X$ and satisfies $Phi'(e)=B$, proving (1). [F3, step 1.3, step 3.1, algebra]

source_lines.135: 1.1 Let U=U(m), I=I_chi. Replace x by y=x−chi(x). These shifted generators have the original brackets, because chi vanishes on brackets. Choose a basis adapted to the lower-central filtration, with weight w_i the largest lower-central index containing its basis vector. PBW reordering and the commutator formula show that I^n is spanned by ordered monomials of total lower-central weight≥n: one inclusion follows from reordering n factors, while the reverse follows because each basis vector of weight w lies in I^w, being a linear combination of iterated brackets of length w. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]
source_lines.137: 1.2 The Rees algebra R=⊕_(n≥0) I^n t^n is generated by y_i t^r, 0≤r≤w_i. Their span is a finite-dimensional Lie algebra: a nonzero bracket component y_k has w_k≥w_i+w_j, so r+s≤w_k. PBW gives its enveloping algebra a polynomial associated graded. For any left ideal, Hilbert basis gives finitely many generators of its homogeneous leading ideal; lift them and subtract matching highest-degree terms until the nonnegative degree decreases to zero. The lifts generate the original ideal. Thus the enveloping algebra is left noetherian, and its surjection onto R makes R left noetherian. For a left ideal J⊂U, ⊕(J∩I^n)t^n is a graded left ideal of R and has finitely many homogeneous generators. For fixed k, choosing n greater than k plus their largest degrees gives J∩I^n⊂I^k J. This is the precise Artin–Rees consequence needed here. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]
source_lines.139: 1.3 Set E_chi=∪_(n≥0)(U/I^n)^*, with left action (x f)(r)=f(r x). To prove injectivity, take a U-linear map phi:J→E_chi. U is noetherian, so choose finitely many generators of J. A common I^k kills their images and hence all images, since I is two-sided. The scalar functional lambda(j)=phi(j)(1) kills I^k J. Choose n with J∩I^n⊂I^k J, extend lambda from J/(J∩I^n) to U/I^n, and call the extension a∈E_chi. The map U→E_chi, u↦u a, extends phi, because at r its value on j is a(rj)=phi(rj)(1)=phi(j)(r). Baer's criterion gives injectivity. This supplies the injective-continuous-dual assertion cited without proof in BK Lemma8.20. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

For a fixed u∈U(g), the finite PBW subspace generated by all iterated ad m on u is finite-dimensional and its negative-column action is nilpotent; sufficiently long products of ad m vanish. Moving u past a product of sufficiently many shifted m generators therefore leaves at least n of them on the left. Equivalently u I^(n+C)⊂I^n U(g) for some C=C(u). Thus lambda u kills I^(n+C)X. source_lines.34: **Given:** A symmetric group $S_n$, the real type-$A$ Soergel category of [[def-real-type-a-soergel-category-and-scalar-extension]] with its normalized indecomposables $B_w^R$ and their characters, the type-$A$ Hecke algebra with its standard basis $H_w$ and Kazhdan-Lusztig basis $\underline H_w$ ([[lem-type-a-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-has-elementary-triangular-bar-properties]]), the statement $\mathrm S(w):\operatorname{ch}(B_w^R)=\underline H_w$ and the hypotheses $\mathrm hL(w)$, $\mathrm{HR}(w)$ of the dictionary ([[def-primitive-subspaces-hard-lefschetz-and-hodge-riemann-signs]]), and the deformed operator $L_\zeta$ on $B_x^RB_s^R$ ([[def-the-deformed-lefschetz-operator-on-b-x-b-s]]).
source_lines.40: [F3] Descent: if $xs<x$ and $\mathrm S(x)$ holds, then $B_xB_s=B_x(1)\oplus B_x(-1)$ and the reduced operator is the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}\rho\cdot(-)&0\\ \zeta\rho(\alpha_s^\vee)&\rho\cdot(-)\end{pmatrix}$; if in addition $\mathrm hL(x)$ holds and $\zeta>0$ then $\mathrm hL(x,s)_\zeta$ holds, while centered hard Lefschetz fails at $\zeta=0$ ([[lem-right-descent-soergel-bimodules-descend-to-simple-invariants-under-the-character-hypothesis]], [[thm-deformed-hard-lefschetz-for-b-x-b-s]]).
